section.title: Trapping a Python Exception
section.para: You want to handle a Python exception in Rexx code.

How it works. A Python exception is the Rexx condition SYNTAX 98.900, so a block with a catch co = syntax clause traps it, as any Rexx error: Rexx's do ... catch ... end is Python's try ... except. (The legacy way, signal on syntax and a label, traps it too.) Its message is Python error: and Python's own. The condition object carries more, in its ADDITIONAL Array: additional[2] is the exception itself, a Python object, whose type and arguments can be looked at, and additional[3] Python's traceback, as text.

The other way works too: .py~raise(.py~KeyError, "missing") raises a Python exception from Rexx code, and a Python exception that goes through Rexx code back to Python is raised there as itself ( uses it to end a sequence).
See also Reference, Errors and Conditions.

section.title: Throwing a Condition through Python
section.para: You want Rexx code that Python calls (a key function, a callback) to stop the whole operation with a condition of your own, or Python code to tell Rexx what went wrong with a Rexx condition.

How it works. Rexx's THROW is Python's raise: a thrown condition goes from caller to caller until a catch clause catches it, and Python between two of those callers does not stop it. Here price throws while Python's map calls it for sum; total, which called Python, has no catch clause, so the condition goes on to the block that called total. (A condition raised with RAISE would stop in total, one level above the call, as Rexx's raised conditions do.) From Python, oorexx.throw(condition, rc, description, additional) throws a Rexx condition with THROW's options: in Python it is an exception, an oorexx.RexxError, and in the Rexx code that called Python it is the condition, thrown.
